modules.title: Getting Started
modules.summary: Sign in, open a project, find your way around, and connect the project folder.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body:
Open **app.superior-fx.com** in **Chrome or Edge**. Other browsers can't connect to project folders, so uploads and folder creation won't work in them.

- **First time?** Click **New here? Create an account** and sign up with the **same email you were invited with**.
- Click the confirmation link in the email, then come back and sign in.
- If you signed up without an invite, a supervisor or Admin has to grant you access on **Team & Access** before you can get in.

steps.title: Open a project
steps.body:
The **Home** page lists **Your projects** down the sidebar. Click one to open it.

Everything you see after that (shots, tasks, reviews) belongs to that project. To switch shows, click **← Projects** at the top of the sidebar.

steps.title: Find your way around
steps.body:
The sidebar is grouped by department:

- **Dashboard**: a company-wide snapshot of every project.
- **Post-Production**: **Post Reports** (scenes, shots, tasks, ingest, artists), **Review & Dailies**, and **Shot Board**.
- **Artist Portal**: **Artist Report**, **Upload Shot**, and **Shot Viewer**.
- **Reference**: checklists, reference docs, and this guide.
- **Admin**: **Team & Access** (supervisors, producers, and Admins only).

Click a group's header to expand or collapse it; the app remembers what you left open. **Pre-Production** and **Production** show a 🔒 and are locked for now. Artist accounts only see the **Artist Portal** and **Reference**.

steps.title: Connect the project folder
steps.body:
Shots, plates, and renders live in the show's folder on disk (for GOTP, the **GOTP** folder on Google Drive). The browser needs your permission to use it.

- If you see **Project folder isn't connected in this browser**, click **Reconnect Folder…** and pick the show folder itself (e.g. **GOTP**), then click **Allow** when Chrome asks.
- After a Chrome restart you may see **Chrome needs your OK to use the project folder** instead. Just click **Allow Access**.

Reconnecting never creates a new folder, so it's always safe to click.

steps.title: How sharing works
steps.body:
Shot, task, and note changes save to the cloud and show up for everyone **live**. There's no Save-to-server step.

Video files and plates travel through **Google Drive**, so a brand-new upload can take a minute to reach another computer. If you see **Still syncing from Google Drive**, wait; the app retries on its own.

modules.title: Setting Up a Project
modules.summary: Create a show, build the artist roster, and lay out scenes and shots.

steps.title: Create a project
steps.body:
On **Home**, click **+** next to **Your projects**.

1. Type the **project name** (e.g. *The Girl on the Plane*). A **show code** fills in automatically; edit it if you like (3–4 letters, e.g. **GOTP**).
2. Optionally set a **Delivery date**. The Dashboard counts down to it.
3. Click **Choose Destination Folder…** and pick where the show folder should be created.
4. Click **Create Project**.

steps.title: Build the artist roster
steps.body:
Go to **Post Reports → Artists** and click **+ Add Artist**.

- Enter the artist's name.
- Under **Tasks this artist can take**, tick every task type they're approved for (Compositing, Roto / Paint, DMP, and so on).
- Click **Save**.

This matters: when you assign a task, the dropdown **only lists artists approved for that task type**. Use the pencil to edit an artist later. Renaming an artist updates their name everywhere it's used.

steps.title: Add scenes
steps.body:
On **Post Reports → Shots**, click **+ Add Scene** and enter the scene number (e.g. **9**, saved as **SC009**).

If the project folder is connected, the scene's folder is created on disk right away. Otherwise you'll see a **Create folder** button on the scene to do it later. Use the pencil next to **SC###** to rename a scene; its folder is renamed too.

steps.title: Add and describe shots
steps.body:
Inside a scene, click **+ Add Shot**, then click the shot's **Edit** (pencil) button:

- Replace **NEW_SHOT** with the real shot code.
- **Script / client description**: what the script or client asked for.
- **Internal description**: what the shot actually needs.
- Set **Complexity**, **Story importance**, **Due date**, and **Pipeline** (Traditional, Hybrid, or AI-assist).

Click **Create folders** to build the shot's folder structure on disk. If you change the shot code afterwards, a **Create folder for new code** button appears. Use the **Collapse/Expand** control to tidy long scenes.

steps.title: Attach a plate to a shot
steps.body:
While editing a shot, use **Import plate video…** or **Import plate sequence…**. The app copies the plate into the shot folder and makes a review proxy and thumbnail.

To bring in many plates at once, use the **Ingest** tab (next module).

steps.title: Export the shot list
steps.body: Click **Export to Spreadsheet…** at the top of Post Reports to download a styled **.xlsx** of every scene and shot. Open it in Excel or Numbers, or upload it to Google Drive to view it as a Sheet.

modules.title: Ingesting Footage
modules.summary: Bring plates in by the batch and let the app match them to shots.

steps.title: Add files
steps.body:
Go to **Post Reports → Ingest** and click **Add Video Files…** or **Add Folder…** (for image sequences).

File and folder names are matched to shot codes, so name them like **GOTP_SC002_010_plate.mov**. The project folder must be connected first.

steps.title: Check the matches
steps.body:
Each file in the list shows what will happen:

- **No shot matched**: the name didn't match a shot. Rename it or add the shot first.
- **Replaces current plate**: that shot already has a plate and this will replace it.
- **Creates shot folders**: the shot's folders don't exist yet and will be made.

Click **×** to remove anything you don't want ingested.

steps.title: Run the ingest
steps.body:
Click **Ingest N files**. **Keep the page open until it finishes.** Big plates take a while.

Each row ends as **Ingested**, **Ingested, no proxy** (the copy worked but no preview could be made), or **Failed**. Click **Clear Finished** to tidy the list.

The **Ingested footage** section below shows a thumbnail per shot. Supervisors and producers can leave **footage notes** there.

modules.title: Assigning Work
modules.summary: Add tasks to a shot, pick artists or vendors, and push the assignment.

steps.title: Add tasks to a shot
steps.body: Edit the shot and choose a task type from **+ add task** (3D Tracking, Roto / Paint, Compositing, DMP, QC / Delivery, etc.). Add as many as the shot needs. Each type can only be added once per shot.

steps.title: Pick who does it
steps.body:
For each task, choose **In-house** or **Outsourced**:

- **In-house**: pick an artist from the dropdown. Only artists approved for that task type are listed (see *Build the artist roster*).
- **Outsourced**: type the vendor's name.

Click **+** to put more than one artist or vendor on a task, and **×** to remove one.

steps.title: Push the assignment
steps.body:
The shot footer counts **assigned tasks** (e.g. *3/3 tasks assigned*). Once every task has someone, click **Push Assignment**.

Pushing creates each task's folders under the shot's **02_tasks/** and puts the work in the artist's **Artist Report**. The shot then shows a **Pushed** tag. If you change tasks later, click **Re-push Assignment**.

steps.title: Deleting things safely
steps.body:
Scenes, shots, and assignments all delete the same way: click the trash icon and **type DELETE** to confirm.

- If you're not an Admin, this sends a **delete request** instead, and the item shows **Delete requested** until an Admin decides.
- Admins see a **Delete requests — waiting for you** banner with **Approve** and **Decline**.

Folders of deleted items are moved into **zzz_DELETED** inside the show folder, not erased.

modules.title: Artist Workflow
modules.summary: See your assignments, start work, submit versions, and read feedback.

steps.title: Check your assignments
steps.body:
Open **Artist Report**. It lists every shot assigned to you with its description, status, and due date.

If it says **Your account isn't linked to an artist yet**, ask a supervisor to link you on the **Team & Access** page.

steps.title: Start a task
steps.body:
Click **Start** on a task when you begin. Its status changes from **Assigned** to **WIP** so the supervisors know it's moving.

Work in the shot's task folder under **02_tasks/**: put your project files in **project/** and your renders in **render/**. Click **VIEW** to see the shot and its plate in the **Shot Viewer**.

steps.title: Submit a version
steps.body:
Open **Upload Shot**:

1. **Attach to**: pick the shot.
2. **Submitting for**: pick your task.
3. **Proxy version**: a new version number is chosen for you. To replace your latest version instead, click **Approve overwrite**.
4. Click **Upload Video…** or **Upload Image Sequence…** (exr, dpx, png, jpg, tif, or tga). The app makes the review proxy for you.
5. Write a **Version note** (what changed), then click **Submit**.

The task becomes **Pending**, which means it's waiting on a supervisor.

steps.title: Read feedback in the Shot Viewer
steps.body:
**Shot Viewer** plays your submitted proxy alongside any **supe notes** and frame annotations. Use the version picker to look at older versions (they show **Not the latest**) or the **Plate**.

Keys: **space** play/pause, **← / →** step a frame, **[ / ]** jump between annotated frames, **F** full screen.

steps.title: Handle a revision
steps.body:
When a supervisor sends a shot back, the task turns **Needs Revision**. Read their notes in the Shot Viewer, click **Resume** in **Artist Report** (back to **WIP**), make the fixes, and submit a new version from **Upload Shot**.

When a supervisor finals it, the task shows **Final**. You're done.

modules.title: Reviewing & Dailies
modules.summary: Watch submissions, annotate frames, and send work back or final it.

steps.title: Open the review queue
steps.body:
**Review & Dailies** lists every task that's **Pending** or **Comp Approved**. Use **Sort by** to order it by Due date, Artist, Task, Scene, or Date submitted.

You can also jump straight in from **Review →** on a task in Post Reports or the Shot Board.

steps.title: Use the player
steps.body:
- **space** play/pause, **← / →** step one frame
- **F** full screen (Esc to exit)
- Scroll to **zoom**, middle-drag to **pan**, **0** to reset
- Loop / play once, and playback speed

Use the version picker to compare older versions or switch to the **Plate**.

steps.title: Annotate frames
steps.body:
Pause on a frame and draw on it, then type what needs to change in the frame note. Use undo to remove the last stroke, or remove the frame's annotation entirely. **[ / ]** jumps between annotated frames.

For overall feedback, write in **Supe notes** and click **Save note**. The artist sees all of it in their Shot Viewer.

steps.title: Revise or Final
steps.body:
- **Revise** sends it back to the artist as **Needs Revision**.
- **Final** (VFX Supervisors and Admins) marks the task **Final**.
- A **Comp Supervisor** sees **Comp Approve** instead: the task becomes **Comp Approved — awaiting VFX Sup**, and a VFX Supervisor gives the last Final.

Producers can watch and read everything but can't Revise or Final.

steps.title: Look closer with HQ renders
steps.body:
When the normal proxy isn't enough, click **Generate HQ** for a 4K proxy made from the artist's submitted render, or render **6K/8K frames** (a single frame, a frame range, or the full range) for close inspection.

These take time. **Keep the tab open until they finish.** HQ playback is heavier and may stutter on slower machines.

modules.title: Tracking Progress
modules.summary: Read the Dashboard and Shot Board to see where the show stands.

steps.title: The Dashboard
steps.body:
The top row shows company-wide numbers: **Shots in post**, **Awaiting review**, **Needs revision**, **Overdue shots**, and **Finaled this week**. Below that is one row per project with its progress and delivery countdown.

Click a project to drill in: the pipeline, **Shots by scene** (hover a tile for its tasks, click to open it), the **Review queue**, **Artist load**, and **Needs attention**.

steps.title: The Shot Board
steps.body:
The **Shot Board** sorts work into **Bidding**, **In progress**, **Sup review**, and **Final** columns, driven live by each task's status. Cards are grouped by shot; click one to expand its tasks. A red **Revise** tag means a task was sent back.

Use **Review →** to open a submission or **VIEW** to open the shot.

steps.title: Task statuses at a glance
steps.body:
| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Assigned** | Pushed to the artist, not started |
| **WIP** | Artist clicked Start or Resume |
| **Pending** | Submitted, waiting on a supervisor |
| **Comp Approved** | Comp Supervisor approved, waiting on the VFX Supervisor |
| **Needs Revision** | Sent back with notes |
| **Final** | Approved and done |

modules.title: Team & Access
modules.summary: Invite people, set their roles, and link them to the artist roster.

steps.title: Invite someone
steps.body:
Go to **Admin → Team & Access**. Under **Invite someone**, enter their email, pick their roles, and click **Add invite**.

Then tell them to open the app, choose **Create an account**, and sign up with **that exact email**.

steps.title: Choose roles
steps.body:
People can hold more than one role:

- **Admin**: everything, including approving delete requests.
- **VFX Supervisor**: runs projects and gives the final **Final**.
- **Comp Supervisor**: runs projects; their Final is **Comp Approve**.
- **Producer**: runs projects, assignments, and the roster; can't Revise or Final.
- **Artist**: only the Artist Portal and Reference.

You can't change your own roles, and only an Admin can edit an Admin.

steps.title: Link accounts to artists
steps.body:
Every artist account must be linked to their entry in the roster, or their Artist Report and Upload Shot stay empty. Pick their name in the dropdown that reads **Not linked to an artist**.

Add them in **Post Reports → Artists** first if they're not there yet.

steps.title: Grant or remove access
steps.body:
Anyone who signed up without an invite appears at the top. Pick their roles and click **Grant access**.

To take someone off the team, click **Remove access** and confirm. **Cancel invite** withdraws an invite nobody has used yet.

modules.title: Backups & Troubleshooting
modules.summary: Back up the team's data and fix the problems people hit most often.

steps.title: Back up the data
steps.body:
Supervisors and producers can click **Export All Data** on **Home** to save a backup of every project, scene, shot, and the artist roster.

**Import from Backup Folder…** and **Import from File…** replace the team's shared data **for everyone**. Only use them to recover from a real problem.

steps.title: Uploads or folders don't work
steps.body:
- Make sure you're in **Chrome or Edge**.
- Look for the folder banner and click **Reconnect Folder…** or **Allow Access**.
- **This shot's folders haven't been created yet**: a supervisor needs to click **Create folders** on the shot in Post Reports, or push the assignment.

steps.title: A video won't load or my work is missing
steps.body:
- **Still syncing from Google Drive**: the file hasn't reached your computer yet. Wait a minute; it retries on its own.
- **Your account isn't linked to an artist yet**: ask a supervisor to link you on Team & Access.
- **Nothing in my Artist Report**: the shot may not be pushed yet, or you're not approved for that task type in the roster.

steps.title: I can't see a page
steps.body: What you see depends on your role. Artists only get the Artist Portal and Reference, and Team & Access is limited to supervisors, producers, and Admins. Ask an Admin if you need more.
